his_statement: topologie la moins fine ... A∪B
statement: Let T be a closed subset of an arbitrary topological space (S,τ), and σ a topology on T finer than τ|T. There exists a least topology τ* finer than τ inducing σ. his_statement: Restriction is a complete homomorphism on subfigure lattices.
statement: For fixed F′≪F, the map G↦F′|G from subfigures of F to subfigures of F′ is the inverse-image map along the least-receiving-stratum map ~F′→~F. It preserves arbitrary joins and meets inside these complete local lattices, including empty operations.

his_statement: “pré-admissibles”, smallest containing member and separation.
statement: Let A⊆P(M) cover M; suppose for each x the family of A-members containing x has a least member A_x, and x↦A_x is injective. Define y≤x iff y∈A_x. Further closure axioms are needed for an atelier.

his_statement: Polyhedral posets and the duality lemma.
statement: Call I polyhedral if each pair having a common lower bound has an infimum. The four-element interpolation condition is self-dual. If every closed interval in I is inductive for the opposite order, the text derives polyhedrality of I^op from that of I; the reverse implication uses inductivity in I. Finite intervals satisfy both chain conditions. In the dual conclusion “greatest” must read “least upper bound”; otherwise the statement reverses the order.

statement: For a symmetric irreflexive relation on M, define A⊥ and A⊥⊥. Triviality is equivalent to universal compatibility, to M itself being a figure, and to disjointness of every distinct pair. Having ≪=≤ alone is weaker. Mog L1 holds for this example iff the poset is discrete.
computation: No numerical computation; symbolic argument or definition.
fate: The lower-set/intersection/union and principal-ideal mechanisms are classical order theory, represented in Birkhoff1948 Chapter IV §§1,7. The source specializes them to compatible lower sets; our E label concerns that mathematical mechanism and does not claim the word magasin or its full axiom package was already standard. Search record: S03, S04, S10.
present_status: As of 2026-11-19: standard order-theoretic construction, with the stated restriction to existing compatible joins and nonempty intersections.

his_statement: Magma associé à un ensemble ordonné L
statement: For any poset L, take point objects P_x and interval objects S_ab for a<b. Faces of S_ab are its endpoints; open refinement is equality on points, a<x<b for P_x≪°S_ab, and a′≤a<b≤b′ for S_ab≪°S_a′b′. Interior disjointness means strict comparability for two points, x≤a or b≤x for a point/interval, and b≤a′ or b′≤a for two intervals. These formulas satisfy the magasin axioms. Ordinary refinement is containment of the closed endpoint intervals. A literal set-figure realization with nonempty cells requires density, and orthogonality agrees with set disjointness only under further order conditions.

his_statement: “Y-a-t-il une décomposition similaire ... entre spatios ?”
statement: With comorphisms defined as arbitrary-join maps commuting with C and morphisms their orthogonal transposes, ask whether every join map f:L→M factors as h†∘g through some complete ortholattice K, where g:L→K and h:M→K commute with C. The answer is no. Let L=M be the six-element four-atom ortholattice with atoms a,b,c,d, and f(0)=f(a)=0, f(b)=f(c)=f(d)=f(1)=a. This preserves all joins. Any nontrivial K and C-preserving join map h:L→K has zero kernel, hence h†(1)=1; since g(1)=1, such a factorization would give f(1)=1. Trivial K gives the zero composite. Thus no K works.

his_statement: Subdivisions: fiberwise supp°φ^{-1}(X)=X°; total suppG=suppF under Atmag supp².
statement: For G≪F with the monotone least-receiver map φ:G→F, the fiber condition is ∨_{Y:φ(Y)=X}Y°=X° for every X∈F. It implies equality of total supports. Conversely total equality implies every fiber equality when all the open supports of F and G lie in one complete Boolean subortholattice (the pair commensurability condition): the fibers partition the join below mutually orthogonal X°. The written named hypothesis is “Atmag supp²”; its identification with scan119γ² remains an ink/notation question.

his_statement: Equivalent(iii): no Z∈A with Z≪F and ZδG; if divisible, no such locusx.
statement: The source asserts that support equality/fiber coverage is equivalent to absence of an elementary refinement Z≪F internally disjoint from every stratum of G, using Atmag supp²; with divisibility it may test only loci. The forward implication follows from nonzero supports. The converse needs a local supply of refinements detecting a nonzero support remainder; pair commensurability alone does not provide it. A three-stratum atelier with Boolean support lattice violates that converse under bare At1–4 plus all commensurability axioms.

statement: The deleted strengthening asks for the order topology of F to be the quotient of that of G and identifies this with single-pair lifting: for X≤X′ choose Y≤Y′ in the respective fibers.
